newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche BA rules out go-it-alone European flights.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche BA rules out go-it-alone European flights.

text.p: Deutsche BA will resume European services only if it has code-share deals with local airline partners, its incoming managing director said.
Carl Michel, DBA managing director from April 1, said the British Airways subsidiary did not plan any new international routes under a three-year break-even plan.
Deutsche BA has shut down a number of loss-making routes to European capitals which it often flew in recent years in competition to Deutsche Lufthansa AG and other carriers.
It now flies only three feeder routes from Hamburg, Berlin and Munich to London Gatwick in addition to eight domestic German routes.
"New routes are very glamourous but I am not into glamour, I want profits," Michel told Reuters in an interview at the ITB travel show in Berlin this week.
"The three-year business plan does not include any route changes. I do not want to be rushed into opening things up, otherwise we would simply be repeating the mistakes of the past," he added.

Deutsche BA would have to be more than "the third-strongest player" if it flew again to European destinations and so code-share deals with local airlines would be necessary to generate sufficient sales for return legs to Germany, Michel said.

A Munich to Paris Orly flight could, however, be an attractive option at some stage in the future due to the BA takeover of Air Liberte and forthcoming merger with TAT, he added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax:5017
